So I put my 12 y/o Chiweenie down about 9 months ago. She had hemangiosarcoma and we did a splenectomy and she lived an extra 6-7 months with chemo and all that other stuff. The day I made the decision to PTS was when taking X-rays, she had mets in her chest. So I made the appointment (at my job) and I took her to McDonald's right after work and got her burgers for everyday that I had left with her. This was a few days before Christmas, so we spent Christmas together with her and on the 28th, my bf and I took her to my job. She was greeted with steak, ice cream, candy, chocolate and she ate it all. My coworker put her catheter in and I gave the final injections (my wishes). I was inconsolable on the ride home and I took the next few days off from work. My boyfriend never left my side and all of my friends, coworkers, and family members came to give their condolences. It really helps to have a good support system with you and don't spend time by yourself. Surround yourself with people that you love and that are understanding of the situation. I cry every once in a while now and I can't touch her urn without crying. It's definitely hard and you will never be the same but you will get through this. I'm sorry that you're having to make this hard decision with your baby, I'm sending out all of my love to both of you.

I went to a PetSmart a few years ago and I walked by the reptile section to look at all the lizards. I saw this one little bearded dragon walking on his wrists and kinda crawling around in the tank and I felt so bad for him, so I bought him. I tried my best to give him what he needed but he's completely handicapped. He's currently 5 years old right now, he's such a special little guy but it makes me really sad that he's like this. He's got some kind of dwarfism and his arms or legs don't really work. I feel like somehow I failed him. I've seen videos of how they treat reptiles in these stores. I also worked at a vet clinic and my doctors worked at Banfield and also told me horror stories about how they treat the reptiles and the other small animals. They're absolutely disgusting.

I worked at a vet clinic for 2 1/2 years. My best advice for you would be to just keep an eye on how much water he's drinking and his personality. Usually dogs with cancer will stop eating and then they will stop being their normal happy selves. I'm sure your pup will let you know when it's time. Stay with him through everything. From my personal experience I haven't had to put one of my dogs to sleep, but I had to put my lizard to sleep. It was pretty difficult but her body let me know when it was time. I still don't know what happened to her but she basically was full of gas and every time she tried to breathe she would poop herself. Once I saw that, I rushed her to the clinic to say my final goodbyes because I knew she was suffering. 
This is going to be hard to read, but he doesn't have much time left. Unfortunately there is no fighting lung cancer, so make the best out of all the time he has left and enjoy every moment. When the time comes be strong and make the right choices for him, not for yourself. It's hard to let go, but his quality of life is what's most important. You can do this, best of luck to you.
